learning_extracted: A substrate_hash change is not evidence that the EXECUTED code changed -- the premise must be tested, not assumed.

Single process + module-scope binding + no dynamic import freezes the import graph at first use; because a divergence boundary by construction falls after the first cell, the change cannot reach execution.
The generalisable defect from 689d is D2, not D3: an inert arm knob makes a declared-distinct control bit-identical to its sibling, and a conjunctive criterion then degrades silently.

targets.recommended_epistemic_category_note: PRE-2026-08-09 OUT-OF-ENUM LABEL, left as written by user decision at the 2026-09-17 gate. `measurement_test_design_defect` is NOT one of the eight claims.yaml enum values (answer_state / derivational / governance_rule / out_of_domain / standard / substrate_ceiling / substrate_coherence / substrate_conditional). The enum-compliant equivalent for this target is `standard` -- it asserts no epistemic suppression -- with the failure mode carried in prose, which is what this field now does. It is left unchanged rather than normalised for two reasons: nothing is written through to claims.yaml from this target (routing is governance-affirm, no claim change, and MECH-448 already reads `standard`), and its direct sibling failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-689i_2026-07-24 carries the identical value -- normalising this one alone would make the pair inconsistent and imply a corpus cleanliness that does not exist. Corpus-wide as of 2026-09-17: 208 artifacts / 652 targets carry an out-of-enum category. That is chipped as a separate infrastructure finding; it is NOT fixed here.
